skill.name: render-automation
skill.description: Guides agents through Render service, deployment, and project workflows using Rube MCP and current Composio tool schemas.
skill.summary: Run Render service discovery, deployment triggers, status checks, and project listing through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static command-execution and reconnaissance alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced workflow examples, and deployment polling guidance. The skill has a real medium operational risk because it can trigger Render deployments through an authenticated Rube MCP connection. No prompt injection or covert data exfiltration evidence was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Deployment actions can affect live services.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation of the service name, service ID, and cache setting before triggering any deployment.

remediation.issue: The skill depends on a third-party MCP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that Render operations route through Rube MCP and require the user to complete Render authentication.

remediation.issue: Tool schemas may change over time.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the instruction to call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before every workflow and validate required parameters before use.

- `clearCache: true` forces a clean build; takes longer but resolves cache-related issues
- Use `cursor` from response for next page
- Continue until `cursor` is absent or results are empty
- Set `limit` to max (100) for fewer pagination rounds
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Poll at reasonable intervals (10-30 seconds) to avoid rate limits
- Avoid rapid polling; use 10-30 second intervals

content.user_title: Automate Render Deployments with Rube MCP
content.value_statement: Render operations require repeated service lookup, deployment triggers, and status checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for those tasks.
actual_capabilities: Connects to the Render toolkit through Rube MCP after user authentication.
Searches current Rube tool schemas before invoking Render actions.
Lists Render services by name, type, limit, and cursor.
Triggers Render deployments with optional build cache clearing.
Retrieves deployment status and supports asynchronous polling.
Lists Render projects and follows cursor-based pagination.
limitations: Requires an active Render connection in Rube MCP.
Does not create new Render services or edit environment variables.
Can affect live deployments, so users should confirm target services.
Depends on current Rube tool schemas and Render API availability.

use_cases.title: Redeploy a Service
use_cases.description: Trigger a Render deployment after confirming the target service and cache setting.

use_cases.title: Check Deployment Health
use_cases.description: Retrieve deployment status and follow progress until the deployment succeeds or fails.

use_cases.title: Inventory Render Resources
use_cases.description: List services and projects with pagination to understand an account structure.

prompt_templates.title: List Render Services
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Rube MCP to list my Render services. Search tools first, then show names, types, and service IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Redeploy One Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Render service named [service name]. Confirm the service ID with me, then trigger a deploy without clearing cache.

prompt_templates.title: Monitor a Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve status for deploy [deploy ID] on service [service ID]. Poll every 10 to 30 seconds until a terminal state.

prompt_templates.title: Map Projects and Services
prompt_templates.prompt: List Render projects and services. Follow pagination, group services by project, and note recent deployment status where available.

output_examples.input: List all Render web services in my account.
output_examples.output: A service inventory with each service name, service ID, service type, and pagination status.

output_examples.input: Redeploy the production API and monitor it.
output_examples.output: A confirmation step, deploy trigger result, deployment ID, status updates, and final success or failure summary.

output_examples.input: Show my Render projects and related services.
output_examples.output: A grouped project overview with service names, service types, and notes for unassigned services.

best_practices: Search Rube tools before each workflow because schemas can change.
Confirm the target service ID before deployment or cache clearing.
Poll deployment status every 10 to 30 seconds to avoid rate limits.
anti_patterns: Triggering deployments from a guessed service name.
Rapid polling that ignores Render API rate limits.
Treating stale tool schemas as current.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Render API key?
faq.answer: No direct API key is documented. It uses Rube MCP and requires the user to authenticate a Render connection.

faq.question: Can it trigger a production deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It can trigger deployments when the connected Render account has permission, so confirmation is important.

faq.question: Can it create or delete Render services?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflows list services, trigger deployments, retrieve deployments, and list projects.

faq.question: Why should tools be searched first?
faq.answer: Rube tool schemas can change. Searching first helps the agent use current parameters and avoid failed calls.

faq.question: Does it support deployment monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It can retrieve deploy status and poll until the deployment reaches a terminal state.

faq.question: What should users confirm before deployment?
faq.answer: Users should confirm the service name, service ID, target environment, and whether to clear the build cache.
